message.content: {"caption":"A three-round comparison of answers about technology used to protect Indigenous lands in the Amazon.","description":"A text-based diagram has three questions across the top, followed by three answer blocks labeled vertically Iter 0, Iter 1, and Iter 2. A blue horizontal rule separates the questions from the answers, and orange vertical bars mark the iteration blocks. The questions are: Q1, “What kind of sending technology is being used to protect tribal lands in the Amazon?”; Q2, “What tribe uses GPS devices to map lands?”; and Q3, “Why do some tribes use remote sensing technology?” Each block has answers A1, A2, and A3 corresponding to those questions. Iter 0: A1 says drones are used to map and protect the tribes’ lands in the Amazon and has an X; A2 says the Yanomami tribe uses GPS devices to map ancestral lands in the Amazon rainforest and has an X; A3 says some tribes use remote sensing technology to protect their lands from commercial interests and has a check mark. Iter 1: A1 reads “*model response was empty*” and has an X; A2 says the Kayapo tribe uses GPS devices to map ancestral lands in the Amazon rainforest and has an X; A3 says some tribes in the Amazon rainforest use remote sensing technology to map their ancestral lands, helping them better protect their territories from commercial interests, and has a check mark. Iter 2: A1 says remote sensing technology is used to protect tribal lands in the Amazon and has a check mark; A2 says GPS devices used by the Trio Tribe, from the rainforests of southern Suriname, help protect their ancestral lands and has a check mark; A3 says some tribes use remote sensing technology to protect their lands from commercial interests and has a check mark. The marks progress from two Xs and one check in Iter 0, to two Xs and one check in Iter 1, to checks on all three answers in Iter 2. No arrows or other connections are shown.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
